newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN will still strive to admit Burma - Malaysia PM.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN will still strive to admit Burma - Malaysia PM.

text.p: Malaysia's prime minister said on Wednesday the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) would strive to get Burma into the regional grouping despite the imposition of U.S. economic sanctions on Rangoon.
"We're going to work very hard to get Myanmar (Burma) into ASEAN," Mahathir Mohamad said when asked by reporters if Washington's sanctions would affect Burma's impending membership in ASEAN.

The United States said on Tuesday it would ban new investment by American firms in Burma because of what Washington described as deepening political repression by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

ASEAN will decide by July whether to admit Burma, along with Cambodia and Laos, as new members this year. Malaysia is this year's chairman of ASEAN, which also groups Brunei, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

Mahathir, who was stopped by reporters after giving a luncheon speech to businessmen, was asked if Malaysia would protest the sanctions in its capacity as ASEAN chairman. "We'll talk with other ASEAN ministers," he said.

Asked if ASEAN ties with Washington would be affected, he said: "I don't know. I can't predict what ASEAN will say." Some diplomats believe the latest sanctions would add to the considerable international pressure mounted on ASEAN not to admit Burma. But the group said it follows a policy of "constructive engagement" with Rangoon and in any case never interferes in the politics of another nation.
